questions.question: Which part of a component tells Angular the HTML tag used to place it in another template?
questions.explanation: The `selector` in the `@Component` metadata (for example `app-expense-row`) is the tag other templates use to render the component.

questions.question: In `<button (click)="addExpense()">`, what kind of binding is `(click)`?
questions.explanation: Parentheses listen for an event coming out of the DOM and call a class method; square brackets push data into the DOM.

questions.question: Why does a component call `inject(ExpenseService)` instead of `new ExpenseService()`?
options: So Angular's dependency injection supplies a shared instance that tests can easily replace
Because `new` is not allowed in TypeScript
So the service runs on the server
questions.explanation: DI hands out a shared instance (here app-wide via providedIn root) and makes swapping in a fake for tests straightforward.

questions.question: Given `const count = signal(0); const doubled = computed(() => count() * 2); count.set(5);`, what does `doubled()` return?
questions.explanation: `computed` re-derives its value from the signals it reads, so after `count` becomes 5, `doubled()` returns 10.
